Calculating your effort range is made easy in Zero to 5K. Your age is a good estimator to calculate your optimal effort level. 
Your max heart rate = 220 - your age
Optimal effort range is 75% - 90% of max heart rate.

Bring your logged training over from Strong or Hevy. Export a CSV and Loadex reads the sessions, sets and exercises, matches them to its own library, and skips duplicates.

LOGGING

Set, rep and weight entry built for speed. Rest timers keep running through a locked screen. Supersets and circuits, warm-up and plate calculators, and a full history with per-exercise records.

RUNNING

EXERCISES

Over 1,000 exercises with muscle maps and instructions. Create your own with custom equipment, muscles and tracking.

AUTO-PROGRESSION

Pick a scheme per exercise (Linear, Double Progression, Percentage-Wave, Top Set and Back-off, or Manual). Loadex writes next session's weight and rep targets onto your workout when you finish. The Progression Report shows what advanced, what held, and where a lift has stalled.

INSIGHTS

A weekly muscle heatmap, sets by body part, weekly volume against published MEV/MAV/MRV ranges, strength trajectory per lift, muscle balance ratios, effective volume by logged RIR, consistency, bodyweight and energy trends.

READINESS

Connect Apple Health and Loadex reads your sleep, HRV, resting heart rate and respiratory rate, scores each against your own baseline, and flags when today's intensity is worth easing. A one-tap daily check-in works with no wearable. Target adjustments are opt-in and reversible.

CALORIES

An EPOC-based estimate that accounts for the afterburn of resistance training, written back to Apple Health.

CONDITIONING AND STRETCHING

A circuit routed around the muscle groups your lifting is about to fatigue, plus stretches for the ones you just trained. Generated before you lift and locked for the session.

COACH

A weekly or monthly review of your logged training in plain language: new records, what is trending, and what to try next. It names only lifts you have performed.

PRIVACY

Your training is stored on your device. Health data is read through Apple Health and is never sold. It leaves your device only when you sign in and back up, and there is no automatic cloud sync.

FREE AND PRO

Free includes 4 workout blueprints, 1 program folder, unlimited history, recorded runs and cardio import, the Linear and Manual schemes, the record side of Insights, and two conditioning blocks a week.

Pro removes the blueprint and program limits, adds the Double Progression, Percentage-Wave and Top Set and Back-off schemes with an RIR floor, unlimited conditioning, the Coach review, workload and monotony tracking, recovery correlation and next-session guidance.

Runs and heart rate arrive from Health on their own: Apple Watch, Polar, Garmin, COROS. You do not have to run "inside the app" - train the way you already train.

The coach reads the whole run, not four averages: heart rate minute by minute, splits per kilometre, pauses, cadence, elevation. That is how it spots a run that cost you, when the average pace looks fine.

IT EXPLAINS EVERY CALL

Ask why zone 3 and not zone 2, and you get the numbers the decision was built on. Disagree and say so: the coach recalculates, or explains why it stands its ground.

It remembers your goal, your history and your last conversation. It does not praise for the sake of praise - it will say "rest today" when that is the right answer.

YOU CAN SEE IF YOU ARE ON TRACK

The forecast shows the result you are on for today and whether you make your date. As a range, not one flattering number. If you are behind, it says so.

YOU KNOW WHAT TO DO TODAY

The home screen answers one question: train or rest. Today's readiness is built from your form, last night's sleep and heart rate variability, and every signal shows the norm it was measured against.

A PLAN YOU CAN FIND YOURSELF IN

The goal is broken into phases and weeks: where you are, what is done, what is ahead. Every session is written out in intervals with a target heart rate. After a run, a debrief: what worked, what to fix.

COMING BACK IS CHEAP

Illness, travel, a bad month at work. The coach recalculates from the shape you are in today instead of sending you back to the start.

WHO IT IS FOR

You are not in your first season. You have a watch that records heart rate. You have a goal with a time and a date. You have tried bought plans and asked ChatGPT - but a plan does not change after your illness, and ChatGPT cannot see your heart rate from the last eight weeks.

Cadence is my personal hobby app (me and my run club). No ads. No in app purchases. No sign up

Runners aim for roughly 170–180 steps per minute to shorten stride and reduce overstriding. Holding an unfamiliar cadence is hard — metronome apps are joyless, and "150 BPM playlists" are approximate and never match your number.

Cadence makes the music itself the pacing device. Pick a target cadence and the beat locks to it, with a sample-accurate metronome underneath.

AUTO SPM BY PACE
Turn on Auto SPM and stop thinking about numbers entirely. Your target cadence follows your live running pace through pace bands you control — slow down for a hill or a breather and the music eases with you; pick it back up and the beat rises to meet you. Fully editable: decide exactly which cadence kicks in at every pace, from easy jog to all-out sprint.

TWO WAYS TO GET YOUR MUSIC
- Free Music: AI generated original tracks across 10 running-tuned genres, streaming from the cloud and growing over time. Every song retunes in real time (pitch-preserving time-stretch) to your exact cadence — any tempo from 150–200 SPM in steps of 5, so you're never stuck with the "nearest" beat.
- Apple Music (optional): connect your subscription and Cadence picks songs whose tempo already matches your target, played through your own account. Requires an active Apple Music subscription.

RUN WITH REAL FEEDBACK
- A redesigned run screen: target and live cadence pinned up top, with a swipe between your now-playing song and a full panel of stats — elapsed, distance, live and average pace, average SPM
- A sample-accurate metronome that clicks right on the beat — 6 sounds, 5 volume levels
- An execution score after every run — the percent of time you held at or above target — saved to your private run history
- An optional voice coach that calls out your cadence if you drift under target, announces your splits, and confirms Auto SPM changes
- Pause tracking on walk breaks, so a breather doesn't dent your stats
- A Lock Screen Live Activity and Dynamic Island — pace, cadence, and controls without unlocking

BUILT FOR RUNNING
- Free Music works fully offline: bundled starter tracks plus up to 200 MB of cached songs, with an OFFLINE badge so you always know what's playable
- Keeps playing when your phone locks; pause, resume, and skip from your AirPods or Lock Screen
- KM or miles, night mode or light — your call

YOUR DATA STAYS YOURS
Run history never leaves your phone. Analytics are private and anonymous — we don't know who you are, only that the app works.

Just a target cadence, a genre you like, and a run.

Most pace calculators assume you’ll run the same pace for the entire race. Real races rarely work that way.

True Pace helps you build a race plan with paces that can vary by mile or kilometer, so you can see how hills, fueling, fatigue, strategy, and late-race surges affect your finish time.

With True Pace 4.5, race planning can also include the course itself. Choose from an included library of selected major race courses, see the course outline and elevation profile, and build a Course-aware pacing plan that adjusts your target splits for climbs and descents. For your own races, you can attach a GPX file to add a course outline, elevation details, and, when usable elevation data is available, Course-aware pacing.

With True Pace you can:

• Plan even, positive, negative, step-based, or Course-aware pacing strategies
• Choose an included race course and start planning faster
• Import GPX files for custom race courses
• See course outlines, elevation profiles, total gain/loss, and per-split elevation
• Adjust individual miles or kilometers
• Send your race or training-run pace targets to the Workout app on Apple Watch
• Compare different race plans without starting over
• Account for hills, water stops, fueling, and key course landmarks
• See your pacing plan visually with an interactive Paceline graph
• Add notes to any split
• Export or print race plans as PDFs
• Share saved races with friends, coaches, or other True Pace users
• Plan common race distances including 5K, 10K, 10 mile, half marathon, marathon, and custom distances

Course-Aware Pacing

Course-aware pacing starts with your flat-equivalent pace, then adjusts your split targets based on the course profile. Use it to understand where a hilly course may naturally slow you down, where descents may help, and how those changes affect your estimated finish time.

Course Profiles

Included race courses can show the shape of the course, elevation gain and loss, and elevation details for each split. If you are planning a local race, trail race, or any event that is not in the included library, you can attach a GPX file from Files.

Pacing Strategies

True Pace makes it easy to test different ways to run the same race. Want to know what happens if you run steady through mile 20, then pick up the pace for the final 10K? Want to compare that against starting more conservatively and getting faster every few miles? True Pace lets you build, duplicate, and adjust those plans with very little data entry.

Paceline

The Paceline graph gives you a quick visual view of how your pace changes over the course of the race. For races with course data, you can also show elevation on the graph, then swipe across it to inspect individual splits and understand exactly where your plan gets faster, slower, climbs, or descends.

Race Notes

Add notes to any mile or kilometer so your plan includes more than numbers. Mark climbs, turns, water stops, gels, landmarks, or reminders for the moments you know will matter.

Sharing and Printing

Saved races can be shared with other True Pace users, sent to friends or coaches, exported as PDFs, or printed for race day.

True Pace was built by an independent runner who wanted a better way to plan races than spreadsheets and generic calculators. You can use the app for free, with a one-time purchase available if you want to save unlimited races.
